title: PACT Mandate
description: Handler-signed capability grant (PACT Specification §19.2) — the RFC #14 shape, verbatim. Attests that the identified handler HumanPrincipal authorized THIS AGENT, WITHIN THESE BOUNDS, UNTIL THIS TIME. Carried untouched (MCP: _meta["au.tailor.pact/mandate"], §20.1); carriers MUST NOT add, remove, or rewrite fields — the §20.3 signature covers the RFC 8785 canonical encoding of the body with the `signature` member absent, so drift breaks verification. SCOPE (§19.1, normative): a verified Mandate is a protocol-level grant only. It is NOT an authorization_proof and MUST NOT be accepted in place of one; it MUST NOT release the §25.6 apply guard on an external-irreversible effect; and per §17.14 / §25.3 it establishes no legal identity, capacity, or authority to bind an entity.

version.description: Mandate shape version. This revision defines "1".

session_id.description: The Parley (§21) or session this Mandate is scoped to. Outside the issuing fabric the scope is advisory (§20.1) — recorded, never the sole rejection ground. Enforcement counters are keyed by the digest of the canonical body, NOT by this client-chosen value (§19.4).

handler_principal_id.description: The handler — the §17.4 HumanPrincipal (W3C DID, strictly 1:1 with a human) granting the authority. Verifiers MUST support `did:web` and `did:key`.

identity_claim.description: Human-readable assertion of what the agent represents. Informational only — like the §17.5 persona claim, it MUST NOT be used in any access-control, trust, or identity decision.

may_publish.description: Categories the agent may publish into. When present, an out-of-category publish MUST be rejected, and an uncategorised publish on a surface that can carry a category MUST be rejected (fail closed — §19.5 check 1). Absent = no category restriction from this Mandate.

must_respect.description: Natural-language boundary assertions. Carried for the human at the escalation point and for the record — NOT machine-evaluable; implementations MUST NOT claim to enforce them (§19.5).

commitment_authority.description: Caps on binding decisions (§19.4). Exceeding it escalates — never rejects (§19.5 check 2, §20.6).

max_binding_decisions.description: Cap on binding decisions taken under this Mandate. Counters MUST be derived from durable records to claim enforcement, are keyed by the canonical-body digest, and commit only on the SUCCESS of the operation they authorize (§19.4).

binding_scope.description: Human-readable scope of the binding authority. Advisory outside the issuing fabric (§20.1).

disclosure_ceiling.description: Maximum §10.3 graduated-disclosure level (1–4) this Mandate allows the agent to reveal. Composes with clearances: the effective limit is the LOWER of this ceiling and what §10.3 / §17.13 already permit. Above-ceiling content MUST be redacted (flagged `redacted: true`) or escalated, never returned unredacted (§19.5 check 3).

escalation_hook.description: Push endpoint where outcomes and mandate-violation events are delivered. The signed delivery format is reserved (§22); until it lands, delivery is implementation-defined and MUST be reported truthfully (§20.6 `escalation_hook_notified`).

expires_at.description: Expiry instant (ISO 8601), evaluated against the RECEIVING implementation's clock — server clock is authoritative (RFC #14 Q6, ratified; §19.3). Skew tolerance reuses the §17.7 window (default ±5 minutes). The body carries no client-time field; no skew check applies to the body itself.

signature.description: Base64url (unpadded) signature over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON encoding of this body with the `signature` member absent, per the §20.3 suite (Ed25519 / `EdDSA` baseline; `ES256` / `ES384` MAY be accepted; symmetric algorithms MUST be rejected). Produced by the handler's enrolled credential — implementations carry pre-signed Mandates and MUST NOT mint or sign one (§19.3).

signing_key_id.description: DID URL of the handler credential that produced `signature` (e.g. `did:web:knox.example#key-1`); SHOULD carry the verification-method fragment. Resolved via the handler principal's credential-registry entry (§17.8) or DID Document (§17.4 pinning applies). An unenrolled key MUST be rejected — fail closed (§20.3); a revoked credential or tombstoned principal MUST be rejected.

examples.identity_claim: this agent represents Knox on API contract negotiation

must_respect.boundary: no breaking changes to event v1 schema
